items.stem: What are the two ways to add staff to a Standalone Group?

options.text: By an HR-attribute rule, or by adding a staff member directly with a start/end date
By importing from HRAD, or by emailing the Help Desk
By composing other groups, or by deriving membership from a parent group
By editing the AuditLog, or by typing into appsettings.json

items.explanation: Standalone Group membership is curated directly: either Rule-based (driven by HR attributes) or Staff-based (a named staff member added with a start and end date).

misconceptions.b: Standalone groups aren't imported from a system of record, and the Help Desk uses the menu itself, not email, to manage them.
misconceptions.c: Composing/deriving is how other group types work; a standalone group is curated by hand.
misconceptions.d: Editing logs/config isn't how membership is set; the old JSON config is being replaced by this SDM functionality.

items.stem: How is a Standalone Group's membership maintained, compared with composed/derived groups?

options.text: It is curated directly in SDM, rather than rolling up from other groups
It is computed automatically by rolling up other groups, just like composed groups
It is maintained upstream in HRAD and only viewed in SDM
It cannot be viewed at all once the group is created

items.explanation: Unlike composed/derived groups whose membership rolls up from other groups, a standalone group's membership is curated by hand directly in SDM. View options let you see that membership.

misconceptions.b: That describes composed/derived groups; standalone groups are curated directly.
misconceptions.c: Standalone groups are owned by SDM, not maintained in a system of record.
misconceptions.d: View options exist specifically to see a group's membership.

items.stem: How does a Standalone Group connect to SDM's authorization (the DA-* groups from S1.3)?

options.text: A standalone group can be set up with linkage to a DA-* AAD group
A standalone group replaces the OIDC token entirely
A standalone group is the same thing as a Data Owner group
Standalone groups have no relationship to DA-* groups

items.explanation: A standalone group can be created with ultimate linkage to a DA-* group, so its curated membership feeds the DA-* group claims SDM reads to make authorization decisions.

misconceptions.b: SDM still reads DA-* claims off the OIDC token; the group feeds those claims, it doesn't replace the token.
misconceptions.c: Data Owners are a distinct AAD-backed role family (S1.4); a standalone group is a hand-curated list that can be linked to a DA-* group.
misconceptions.d: Linkage to DA-* groups is a defining feature of standalone groups.

items.stem: The Help Desk needs to give a staff member access to an area for exactly two weeks. Using Standalone Groups, what's the right approach?

options.text: Add the staff member directly to a DA-*-linked group with a start and end date
Define an HR-attribute rule so all staff get the access permanently
Edit the school record to grant the access
Delete the staff member's account and recreate it after two weeks

items.explanation: Staff-based membership with start/end dates is what enables temporary access. Adding the person to a group linked to the right DA-* group, with an end date, grants the access and lets it expire automatically.

misconceptions.b: A rule applies broadly and permanently — wrong tool for one person's two-week need.
misconceptions.c: Schools (S3.1) are an augment-only surface, unrelated to granting access.
misconceptions.d: Account deletion has nothing to do with timed group membership.

items.stem: Which action is legitimate for Standalone Groups but NOT for Schools (S3.1)?

options.text: Creating and deleting the entity in SDM
Writing the change to DDH with an audit trail
Viewing the record in SDM
Editing it without anyone knowing who changed it

items.explanation: SDM owns standalone groups outright and can create and delete them. Schools come from a system of record (HRAD) and are augment-only — SDM never creates or deletes them.

misconceptions.b: Writing to DDH with audit is true of both — it isn't the distinguishing action.
misconceptions.c: Both can be viewed; that isn't unique to standalone groups.
misconceptions.d: All SDM edits carry CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit; silent edits never happen.

items.stem: Where is the role-based access in Standalone Groups being ported from?

options.text: An old JSON config file
The HRAD system of record
The AuditLog table
A SharePoint list that SDM still depends on

items.explanation: This functionality is transitioning from a JSON config file into SDM; the role-based access that used to live there is now managed as Standalone Groups.

misconceptions.b: HRAD is the source of record for schools/staff, not the origin of this config.
misconceptions.c: The AuditLog records changes; it isn't the source being ported in.
misconceptions.d: The data is being ported into SDM from a JSON file, not retained in SharePoint.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain how Standalone Groups let the Help Desk grant temporary access, and name the two ways a group's membership can be filled.
rubric: Names the two membership methods: rule-based (HR attributes) and staff-based (direct add with start/end dates)
Connects temporary access to staff-based membership with an end date and/or linkage to a DA-* group
Notes the access reflects through DA-* group claims (effective at next sign-in) — or that SDM owns/curates these groups directly
items.sampleAnswer: A standalone group is filled either by an HR-attribute rule or by adding a staff member directly with a start and end date. For temporary access, the Help Desk adds the person to a DA-*-linked group with an end date; the membership feeds the DA-* group claims SDM reads, taking effect at the user's next sign-in and expiring on the end date.
